  • The applications are decided by a lottery, and one can be entered more than once. There are companies that exist solely to do this on behalf of a client to increase the odds that they get their prospective employees a much better chance of winning a visa.

  • Companies pretend like they're looking for Americans, or provide entirely impossible situations such that they can turn to the government and say "we can't find the right guy so we want to look overseas."

  • There are more STEM graduates than STEM job openings, and these openings (by my own speculation) are mostly filled by networking and cronyism instead of looking for talent in classifieds or open applications.
